newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina would only make NAFTA move with Mercosur.
newsitem.headline: Argentina would only make NAFTA move with Mercosur.

text.p: Argentina would only seek membership in the North American Free Trade Agreement as part of a Mercosur block bid, President Carlos Menem said Monday.

Argentina's neighbor Chile has already been earmarked as the next likely member of NAFTA, which currently groups the United States, Canada and Mexico. However, Chile's entry has been bogged down by opposition in the U.S. Congress.
Argentine officials have recently had to deny reports that Argentina was seeking NAFTA entry, and Menem emphasized that his country "has not held talks with NAFTA over its entry."

"The only negotiations there could be would not be between Argentina and NAFTA, but between Mercosur and NAFTA," he told a small group of foreign journalists on the eve of a visit to the United States.

The Peronist president made clear Argentina's priority is Mercosur, the customs bloc launched in 1995 grouping Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile is an associate member and Bolivia on the way to a similar associate status.
Menem said the trade integration of all of the Americas would be reached "much more easily and quickly" via existing trade blocs such as Mercosur, NAFTA and the Andean Pact.
"I have said with a touch of humor that really we should ask NAFTA when it wants to join Mercosur," he said.
